params.body:
Fourth measurement to carry verdicts, after `deployed`, `app` and the keys.

| facet | thresholds, worst first |
| --- | --- |
| reachable | `IS_DOWN` (status outside 200..399, now), `IS_UP` (ok) |
| certificate | `TLS_CRITICAL` (<8 days, now), `TLS_EXPIRING` (<21, week), `TLS_HEALTHY` (ok) |

`IS_UP` was always the one truth about "up"; `IS_DOWN` is its complement, through a new operator `outside` in `Thresholds::reaches()` and in `Report\Gate`, so that down is a word Elixir says rather than the absence of one. A site that does not answer (status 0) is down the same way. The 8 is Portal's card number, copied; 21 was already here.

No certificate is no verdict on it (plain http, or a certificate we failed to read), as the facts already worked.

Tests: six cases in `SiteScanTest`; the catalogue test and the "no level" test moved to `dns`, which still does not judge. Suite 599 green, PHPStan and Pint clean. Portal follows: the Site card reads `reachable` and `certificate`, and `ElixirRegistry` learns `outside` for the day it reads such an entry.
params.title: Site judges its own facts: up or down, and how long the certificate holds
